verdict_reasoning: The decisive objection is demand-1. Message #1 names no user, tool or report that needs the overview, and a user-defined `union all` over the existing progress views returns the same rows. The cost of the view is low, so this is "not now, show demand" and no rejection. The verdict rests on absence of evidence in a one-message thread, so confidence is low.

brief.title: Add pg_stat_progress view listing all backends reporting progress
brief.problem: Finding active progress reports means querying each pg_stat_progress_* view separately. The patch targets users who monitor cluster operations and want to find all of them in one place.
brief.proposed_design: A new system view, pg_stat_progress, has one row per backend reporting command progress, across all databases, with pid, command and progress_view. It is defined in system_views.sql on top of pg_stat_get_progress_info() and the existing progress permissions, with no backend changes. The pg_stat_progress_cluster compatibility view adds no extra row for REPACK, CLUSTER or VACUUM FULL.
user_visible_surface: New system view pg_stat_progress with columns pid (integer), command (text) and progress_view (regclass).
command values: ANALYZE, VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, BASEBACKUP, COPY, REPACK, DATACHECKSUMS; REINDEX shows as CREATE INDEX, CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL as REPACK.
All three columns are visible to all users; details follow the permission rules of the detailed views.
author_claims: The view needs no backend changes and reuses existing progress infrastructure.
pid, command and progress_view are the minimal common fields; datid and datname are left out because base backups cover the whole cluster.
Build, regression, isolation and new TAP tests passed locally.
The longer-term aim is easier discovery of cluster operations and progress reporting for more commands.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible, and nobody has replied. The author asks for feedback on usefulness and columns; CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase.
unclear: The proposal does not say why pg_stat_activity, or a join with it, does not already meet the need.
The patch does not say whether the view must change when a new progress command is added, or how that is kept in sync.
The patch does not say why showing pid and command to all users is safe, when the detailed views limit what other users see.
No use case shows why progress_view as regclass is more useful than the command name alone.

objections.title: No demand shown beyond the author's wish for one overview
objections.failure_scenario: The view is added, and every later progress command must update its definition and docs. Monitoring tools already query the detailed pg_stat_progress_* views they care about, so few of them switch to it. The project carries the upkeep for a view that saves users one union query.
objections.argument: Message #1 gives the problem as an inconvenience and cites no field report, -general thread or tool that asked for this, and no other database's equivalent. A user can write the same three-column result today as a union over the seven detailed views, or over pg_stat_get_progress_info() per command, in a user view. The thread has no replies yet, so nobody else has said they need it. The cost is small, and the benefit is smaller still.
objections.author_must_show: Which monitoring tools or users need this overview today, and why does a user-defined union of the existing progress views not serve them?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 names no user, tool or report asking for the overview, and the thread has no replies. The existing views already show pid for backends in all databases, so a user-defined union returns the same rows.

other_surviving.title: The command column means something different from the same column in the detailed views
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA filters `pg_stat_progress` with `command = 'REINDEX'` or `command = 'CLUSTER'`, as they would in `pg_stat_progress_create_index` or `pg_stat_progress_cluster`, and gets no rows while a REINDEX runs. A monitoring dashboard then reports nothing in progress. The DBA finds the cause only after reading the documentation for the new view.
other_surviving.argument: The existing progress views already have a `command` column, and it holds the command the user ran, such as `REINDEX CONCURRENTLY` or `VACUUM FULL`. The new view reuses the name for a family label: REINDEX shows as `CREATE INDEX`, and CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL show as `REPACK`. Reusing a column name with a different meaning goes against existing practice, and the proposal gives no reason for it. A name like `command_family` or `progress_type`, or values that match the detailed views, would avoid the clash.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why should `pg_stat_progress.command` hold family names when `command` in the detailed progress views holds the command the user ran?

critic.reasoning: The detailed views do hold the command as run: `pg_stat_progress_create_index.command` shows `REINDEX`, and `pg_stat_progress_cluster.command` shows `VACUUM FULL`. The patch documentation gives family labels under the same column name, and message #1 gives no reason.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: New progress commands must also update the overview view
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A later patch adds progress reporting for a new command, with a new ProgressCommandType value and a new pg_stat_progress_* view, but does not edit pg_stat_progress. Backends running that command never appear in the overview. A monitoring user finds out only when a long operation is missing from the dashboard that is supposed to list all operations.
other_surviving.argument: The view is built in system_views.sql on pg_stat_get_progress_info(), and that function takes one command name per call. So the view has to list each command family and its detailed view by hand. Message #1 says the longer-term aim is to add progress reporting to more commands, which makes this edit a recurring one. The material names no test or assertion that fails when a command type is missing from the view, so a reviewer of a later patch would likely miss it.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What makes the build or regression tests fail when a new progress command type is added but pg_stat_progress is not updated?

critic.reasoning: `pg_stat_get_progress_info()` takes one command name per call, so the view has to list each command family by hand. The patch prose names no check that fails when a new command type is left out, and message #1 plans more commands.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: New view instead of a progress column in pg_stat_activity
refuted.failure_scenario: A tool author wants to show what each backend is doing and ends up joining `pg_stat_activity`, `pg_stat_progress` and a detailed view on pid. Later a generic progress view with shared counters is proposed, but the `pg_stat_progress` name is already taken by a three-column index view.
refuted.argument: `pg_stat_activity` already has one row per backend and is where users look for the current activity. A nullable column there, or a function, would give the same lookup without a new catalog view. The bare name `pg_stat_progress` is the most natural name for a later view of shared progress columns such as phase or blocks done. Message #1 compares only with querying each detailed view and does not discuss these alternatives.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a separate view named `pg_stat_progress` better than a progress column in `pg_stat_activity`, and what would a later view with shared counters be called?

critic.reasoning: Progress reporting already lives in separate `pg_stat_progress_*` views that users join to `pg_stat_activity` on pid, so the patch follows existing practice. The name conflict depends on a later proposal that is not in the material, and a view can gain columns later.

refuted.title: A union of the existing progress views already gives this list
refuted.failure_scenario: A monitoring user who wants every active operation can already run one `union all` query across the `pg_stat_progress_*` views, selecting `pid` and a literal command name. After the patch, core carries a permanent view that returns the same rows. Each new progress command then needs a matching change to that view.
refuted.argument: The proposal gives the same pid and command information that a short user query over documented views already returns. It saves one query, and the user no longer has to update that query when a new progress view is added. Message #1 explains why datid was left out but not why the existing views and pg_stat_activity are not enough. A committer would likely ask whether that convenience is worth a new system view that must be kept in sync with every future progress command.
refuted.author_must_show: Which monitoring task needs this view that a `union all` over the existing pg_stat_progress_* views cannot handle, and who has asked for it?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which makes the same `union all` point and also covers the missing evidence of demand.

questions: Which monitoring tools or users need this overview today, and why does a user-defined `union all` over the existing pg_stat_progress_* views not serve them?
Why does a join of pg_stat_activity with the detailed progress views not already meet the need?
What makes the build or the regression tests fail when a new progress command type is added but pg_stat_progress is not updated?
Why does `pg_stat_progress.command` hold family names when `command` in the detailed progress views holds the command the user ran?

committability.owner_note: A committer who knows the progress reporting code and the statistics views in system_views.sql would have to own it. Nobody has replied in the thread.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent system view whose command list and documentation must change with each new progress command. Monitoring tools will depend on its column names and values.
committability.author_follow_up: Message #1 states a longer-term aim to extend progress reporting to more commands, which suggests continued work. CFbot reports the patch needs a rebase and no rebase is visible yet.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A report from a monitoring tool author or from users who need one list of all progress-reporting backends, with a reason why a user-defined union of the existing views is not enough. Support from other list members in the thread would also count.

priority.reason: The patch is about 13 KiB, with one SQL view, documentation and a TAP test, and no backend changes, so review and upkeep are cheap. Message #1 shows no user or tool that needs it, so it can wait until demand is shown.

provisional_note: Without the code I could not check how the view lists the command families, whether the new TAP test catches a missing command type, or whether the view keeps the existing filtering of other users' details.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report checkpoint progress with pg_stat_progress_checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Michael Paquier, Andres Freund, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: The thread started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log. After objections it became a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the checkpoint phase, flags, start LSN, start time and per-phase counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The final close came because the author stopped responding after Andres Freund marked the patch waiting on author for a docs build failure and noted that the architectural feedback had not reached a conclusion. Earlier, Michael Paquier returned it because the view was too complex and carried fields of little use, such as next_flags, start LSN and most flag values. Julien Rouhaud objected that the view showed the initial checkpoint flags instead of how the checkpoint was behaving now. Andres Freund measured progress-update overhead in BufferSync() on large shared_buffers.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: There has been no updates on this thread for some time, so this has been switched as Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Report checkpoint progress with pg_stat_progress_checkpoint
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_progress_checkpoint view that reports the phase, flags, start LSN and other details of the running checkpoint or restartpoint. It started as a proposal to log checkpoint progress in the server log, but reviewers asked for a progress view instead.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with Feedback because the view needed simplification: several fields and flags were of little use for monitoring, and the phase names were too long. Andres Freund objected that the view definition makes pg_rewrite bigger, and he asked for proof that the progress counters do not slow down checkpoints with many dirty buffers. The last measurement shown, a manual checkpoint taking 2.457 s with the patch against 2.334 s without, got no reply.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I think that what's proposed could be simplified, and we had better remove the fields that are not that useful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add index scan progress to pg_stat_progress_vacuum
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds index vacuum progress to pg_stat_progress_vacuum, with counts of indexes to process and indexes processed, including indexes handled by parallel vacuum workers. Later versions keep worker progress in a hash table in the main shared memory segment, so the progress views can read it after a worker exits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Robert Haas objected to the use of the main shared memory segment and to the locking it adds to progress reporting, which is meant to be low overhead. They asked that workers pass data to the leader through the parallel vacuum's dynamic shared memory, and that the leader report it with the existing progress fields; Masahiko Sawada agreed. Greg Stark returned the patch because of these design changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That is, I am imagining that you would want to use DSM to propagate
data from workers back to the leader and then have the leader report
the data using the existing progress-reporting facilities.

precedents_retrieved.title: Progress reporting for COPY command
precedents_retrieved.summary: Progress reporting for COPY command

precedents_retrieved.title: CLUSTER command progress monitor
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_progress_cluster view that reports the phase of CLUSTER and VACUUM FULL, the scan method, and counts of heap tuples scanned. Phases cover heap scan, sort, writing the new heap, file swap, index rebuild and final cleanup, with a combined phase for the index-scan path.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected that the design reports only the phase name for sorting and for the index-scan path, though scanning and writing the new heap take most of the runtime. He also asked to drop heap_tuples_total, which only copies reltuples. The author agreed to rework it, including a sort progress counter, but no new version came before the commitfest closed, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I would guess that scanning the
heap and writing the new heap would ordinarily account for most of the
runtime, or at least enough that you're going to want something more
than just knowing that's the phase you're in.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_stat_activity: avoid showing state=active with wait_event=ClientRead
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_stat_activity read each backend's state and wait event in one pass, so active backends no longer show wait_event ClientRead under high load. It also changes how the local copy of backend status is allocated, using chunks instead of one allocation sized by max_connections.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas argued that the state and the wait event are set by different functions at different times, so any reader can see them out of step and the patch can only narrow the race. He said these lightweight introspection views were never meant to be consistent with each other, and that making them so would add complexity and slow the system down. The thread ends with the authors asking for the patch plus a documentation note, and no reply is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The very best a patch like this can hope to do is narrow the
race condition enough that the discrepancies are observed less
frequently in practice.

precedents_retrieved.title: System username in pg_stat_activity
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an authname column to pg_stat_activity that shows the externally authenticated user name, the same value the SYSTEM_USER keyword returns. It also covers methods such as peer and ident, which have no view of their own like pg_stat_gss.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread stopped in February 2024 during an open discussion about whether pg_stat_activity already has too many columns and should be split into several views. Magnus Hagander replied that moving columns would break existing monitoring tools, and no one answered. Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback in October 2024 because nobody had posted since.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: This is the last message sent on this thread, and an entry was still registered in the CF app, so I am marking that as RwF for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: ANALYZE command progress checker
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_progress_analyze view that reports the phase of a running ANALYZE and counters for blocks and sample rows, using the progress reporting framework that VACUUM uses. Later versions add phases for inherited sample rows and statistics computation, and a child_relid column.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas proposed moving the patch to v11 because it arrived one day before the last CommitFest, the design was not right, and the right design was still unknown. Reviewers found that the reported phases did not match where ANALYZE spends its time, and that counters reset for each child table, so inheritance trees showed wrong progress. Sample-row and block counts were also not reliable, and FDWs had no way to report progress.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It was
submitted one day before the start of the last CommitFest, the design
wasn't really right, and it's not clear even now that we know what the
right design is.

precedents_retrieved.title: Enhance file_fdw to report processed and skipped tuples in COPY progress
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes file_fdw report tuples_processed and tuples_skipped (rows skipped with on_error = 'ignore') in pg_stat_progress_copy. file_fdw already reports relid and bytes_processed there.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch. Each backend has one progress-reporting slot, so a query that scans several file_fdw tables, for example in a join, can report wrong progress. Masahiko Sawada asked whether file_fdw should use COPY progress at all before more fields are added. The author later decided that the patch would make wrong progress views more common, and that the problem already existing was not a reason to add more cases.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don’t think the fact that the issue
already exists is a good reason to introduce more, and likely more common,
scenarios where it could occur.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. [P2] proposed a new checkpoint progress view, so it is a different idea. Its recorded reason was that the view had fields of little use for monitoring, and this three-column view does not share that problem. The thread has one message and points to no earlier discussion of the same idea.
The pg_dump round-trip, GUCs, grammar and behaviour for existing queries are not affected, because the patch adds only a system view.

The proposal adds only a SQL view in system_views.sql and bumps catversion, with no backend, WAL, on-disk, wire protocol or ABI change. The view's catalog footprint is one more pg_rewrite entry, which initdb creates and pg_upgrade does not carry over. Keeping the view in step with new progress commands is a maintenance question for other angles.

The view exposes nothing new to other users, because the detailed pg_stat_progress_* views already show pid and database to everyone and a row's presence shows the command. The view is SQL over pg_stat_get_progress_info() with no new privilege, function or DoS path, though without the code I could not check that it keeps the existing per-backend NULL filtering.
From the maintenance angle there is one objection. The view adds no hot-path cost and no backend changes, and its cost falls only on users who query it.
One objection only. Documented views meet the need with modest effort, so the open point is whether the convenience is worth a permanent view.
One demand objection only. The cost of the view is low, so this reads as "not now, show demand" rather than a rejection.
